result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks with physical obstructions, such as utility poles, and a lack of designated crossing infrastructure at the intersection. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the lack of buffers from moving traffic and poor visibility at corners due to parked cars reduces overall safety.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located directly in the path of the narrow sidewalk on the right side of the image, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around it.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, providing no designated space or priority for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left sides near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten crossing distances, slow turning vehicles, and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalks to meet accessibility standards and relocate utility poles to provide a clear, unobstructed path of travel.

result.summary: The image shows a residential urban street with a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk directly adjacent to multi-story buildings. While the walkway is in good condition, it lacks a buffer from the roadway and is partially obstructed by waste bins.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Waste bins (blue and green) are placed directly in the pedestrian path, narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the sidewalk near the older building entrance.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the travel lane, exposing pedestrians to moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible curb line.

interventions.title: Designated Waste Storage
interventions.description: Provide off-sidewalk or recessed areas for trash bins to keep the walkway clear and accessible.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The residential street provides continuous sidewalks on both sides, but the effective walking width on the left is significantly reduced by utility poles. There is a lack of marked pedestrian crossings, traffic calming, or lane markings, creating an informal environment for crossing.

hazards.name: Utility poles obstructing sidewalk
hazards.description: Large wooden utility poles are situated directly in the path of the left-side sidewalk, creating barriers for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, requiring pedestrians to cross the unmarked roadway without priority.

hazards.name: Degraded roadway surface
hazards.description: The asphalt shows signs of cracking and wear, which can create tripping hazards or uneven surfaces for pedestrians crossing.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian crossing areas and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Sidewalk widening and pole relocation
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk or relocate utility poles to provide a consistent, unobstructed clear path of travel for all users.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a paved sidewalk and a brick buffer zone. The environment is generally well-maintained but lacks pedestrian-specific infrastructure like lighting or marked crossings.

hazards.name: Lack of street lighting
hazards.description: No street lights are visible, which may reduce pedestrian visibility and safety at night.

hazards.name: Debris on walkway
hazards.description: Litter and small debris are present on the sidewalk and in the gutter area.
hazards.location_in_image: On the sidewalk and near the curb in the foreground

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Regular Maintenance
interventions.description: Implement regular street cleaning and litter removal to keep the walkway clear and inviting.
